subject: construction-studies
timingNote: Higher Level Theory paper: 3 hours, 300 marks, answer any five questions of ten at 60 marks each. That is 50% of your grade. The other 50% is made up of two components marked out of 150 each: the Practical Test (a 4 hour woodwork test sat in school in late April, 25%) and the Coursework: Design and Realisation (an artefact plus a design folio, 25%). Ordinary Level is different: the Theory paper is 2 hours 30 minutes and 200 marks (any four questions), so it is 40% of the grade and the practical and the project are 30% each. The percentages are worked out from the marks printed on the SEC papers (600 marks at Higher, 500 at Ordinary). The new Construction Technology course does not affect 2027. It is first examined in 2028. Every mark split below comes from the 2025 and 2024 SEC marking schemes and the 2025 and 2026 papers. There is no compulsory question in 2025 or 2026.

examDay.task: 2025 reference: Friday 13 June, 2:00 to 5:00. You get one question paper with ten questions (some have drawings or plans printed on them) and write in an answerbook. The 2026 paper was sat in June (reported 11 June). The 2027 timetable was not published when this was checked, so check the date when it comes out.
facts: Answer any five of ten questions. All carry equal marks (60 each). Question 1 is the scale drawing question but it is not compulsory in 2025 or 2026.
Five of ten has been the rule on the 2025 and 2026 papers, and one grind-site guide says it holds for 2027. The 2027 instructions are not published yet, so read the front of the paper.
Pencil, scale rule, set squares, compass and eraser for drawings. Write notes in ink. Freehand sketches are expected and marked.

2 hours 30 minutes, 200 marks, any four questions (about 50 marks each). Fewer questions are offered than at Higher Level. We could not open the Ordinary marking scheme, so its mark splits are not listed here.

timeline.label: Choose

timeline.label: Question 1

timeline.label: Question 2
timeline.detail: Second question. Keep to time: move on when the clock says so.

timeline.label: Question 3

sections.name: Theory Paper – Drawing and detailing questions

tips.timing: About 35 minutes per drawing question. Do the drawing first while you are fresh, then the add-on detail.
tips.structure: Drawing questions are marked as a list of items from the scheme, each worth 4 marks (3 for the drawing and 1 for its note), plus 8 marks for scale and drafting.
reminders: Write answers in ink and drawings in pencil (2025 paper instructions)
Note the name, size and material on every layer
All questions carry equal marks, 60 each at Higher Level
Add the extra detail asked for in part (b) to your drawing before you leave the question

questionTypes.name: Scale drawing of a construction detail
questionTypes.where: Question 1 every year in 2024, 2025 and 2026, and sometimes a second drawing question (2025 Q7, chimney stack).
questionTypes.see: 2026 Q1: to 1:10, draw a vertical section through half a slated roof from just below the eaves to the ridge. Show one wall and one rafter, the details from 600 mm below the ceiling joists up, three courses of slate and four dimensions. 2025 Q1(a): to 1:5, a section from the bottom of the strip foundation to 200 mm above the bottom of the window frame, with 1.0 m of floor. 2025 Q7(a): section through a chimney stack and the roof around it.
questionTypes.marked: 2025 Q1(a) was worth 56 of the 60 marks. Foundation and floor 5 items x 4, external wall 4 items x 4, window 3 items x 4. Each 4 marks is 3 for the drawing and 1 for the note. Scale 4 marks and drafting 4 marks are marked on top (Excellent 8, Good 6, Fair 4). Part (b) was 4 marks.
questionTypes.play: Draw the layers in the order the building goes up, from the outside in. Write a size and material on every layer as you draw it. The note is a quarter of each item. Use a pencil and a scale rule and leave room for the add-on detail in (b).
traps: Starting or stopping at the wrong level. 2025 Q1 began at the bottom of the strip foundation and stopped 200 mm above the bottom of the window frame, and anything outside that earns nothing.
Drawing the layer but not naming it. You lose the annotation mark on every item, and the instructions say names, sizes and materials must be noted on the drawing.
Skipping the dimensions the question asks for. 2026 Q1 wanted four typical dimensions.
Drawing too small. The scale and drafting marks (8) are given for clean line work at the stated scale.

questionTypes.name: Add-on detail on the same drawing
questionTypes.where: Part (b) of the Question 1 and Question 7 drawing questions.
questionTypes.see: 2026 Q1(b): airtightness detailing where the ceiling meets the external wall. 2025 Q1(b): detailing to stop radon gas getting in. 2025 Q7(b): stopping rainwater getting between the chimney and the roof. 2024 Q1(b): ventilation of the roof structure.
questionTypes.marked: A small block of 4 to 6 marks (2025 Q1(b) 4, 2025 Q7(b) 6). It is one design detail drawn onto your existing section.
questionTypes.play: Add it in a different line colour or a bold line on the section you already drew. Label the barrier or membrane by name, for example radon barrier, vapour control layer, flashing, and show where it laps.
traps: Leaving it blank because the drawing took too long. It is the cheapest 4 to 6 marks on the paper.
Describing the detail in words only. The question says on your drawing.

questionTypes.name: Best practice detailing at circled locations
questionTypes.where: A question with a house section where several spots are circled. 2025 Q8(b) and 2026 Q9 (thermal bridging at the wall and roof junction); 2026 Q5 (moisture in a timber frame wall).
questionTypes.see: 2025 Q8(a): discuss two benefits of preventing air leakage. 2025 Q8(b): choose three of the circled locations and show the best practice design detailing for each. 2026 Q9 opened with the statement that a continuous thermal envelope prevents thermal bridging, then gave a section of a bungalow with the weak point circled.
questionTypes.marked: 2025 Q8: (a) 12 marks, 6 per benefit (3 for the point, 3 for the discussion). (b) 48 marks, 16 per location: 8 for the notes and 8 for the sketch.
questionTypes.play: Pick the three locations you can draw in your sleep, such as window head, eaves and ground floor edge. For each, write four or five short labelled notes and a clear sketch, and spend equal time on both halves.
traps: Writing a paragraph and a rough sketch. The scheme gives the sketch the same marks as the notes.
Choosing a location you have not practised just because it comes first on the page.

questionTypes.name: Services layout diagram
questionTypes.where: 2025 Q9 (lighting circuit) and 2024 Q8 (hot water and central heating); 2026 Q8 began with a first-floor bedroom and en-suite bathroom.
questionTypes.see: 2025 Q9(a): the wiring layout for two light points controlled by one switch. (b) Two safety features of the design. (c) Two ways to reduce electricity use. 2024 Q8(a): a layout for hot water and central heating.
questionTypes.marked: 2025 Q9(a) 34 marks: six items worth 5 each (distribution board, switch, two light points, live, neutral and earth cable), each 4 for the drawing and 1 for the note, plus 4 for cable size (1) and cable colour (3). (b) 16 marks, notes 4 and sketch 4 per feature. (c) 10 marks, 2 for the point and 3 for the discussion each.
questionTypes.play: Learn one standard diagram for each service until you can draw it with the labels. Colour the live, neutral and earth cables and write their sizes.
traps: Forgetting the cable colours and sizes. In 2025 they were worth 4 marks.
Showing the cable runs but no distribution board. The board was a full 5 marks.

sections.name: Theory Paper – Design, calculation and discussion questions

tips.timing: About 35 minutes per question. Do the sketch halves as you go, not at the end.
tips.structure: Almost every part is a point plus a sketch or a point plus a discussion. Marks come in small blocks of 2, 3, 5 and 6, so lots of short, specific answers beat one long one.
reminders: Use neat freehand sketches to illustrate written descriptions
Number the question before each answer
Dimensions and materials on sketches earn the extra marks
Answer exactly the number asked: two benefits means two

questionTypes.name: Layout redesign or extension
questionTypes.where: Question 3 every year (2024 renovation, 2025 garage conversion, 2026 extension to a 1920s farmhouse).
questionTypes.see: 2026 Q3: a single-storey extension of no more than 15 square metres to a farmhouse, with an open-plan kitchen, dining and living area, better daylight and a ground-floor bedroom and bathroom. (a) show the revised layout, (b) three reasons, (c) two benefits of changing the layout. 2025 Q3: convert a garage, revise the ground floor, then design the outside of the garage.
questionTypes.marked: 2025 Q3: (a) 22 marks, 16 for the layout and 2 each for the bathroom, the open-plan space and the daylight. (b) 18 marks, 6 per reason. (c) 20 marks, 10 notes and 10 sketch.
questionTypes.play: Tick each requirement in the question in the margin as you draw it. The three extra requirements are 6 easy marks. Write each reason as a full point plus its link to the owners, for example daylight and lower heating bills.
traps: Missing one of the named requirements. Each one is a separate 2 marks.
Ignoring the limit in the question, such as 15 square metres or the load-bearing wall B-B in 2026 Q3. The layout is marked against the brief.
Giving a reason with no discussion. Reasons are marked as a point plus a discussion.

questionTypes.name: Lifetime use, health and safety
questionTypes.where: Question 2 every year (2024 and 2026 lifetime use; 2025 construction site health and safety).
questionTypes.see: 2026 Q2: two best practice guidelines for lifetime use at each of the entrance and the bathroom, then three considerations for a garage conversion for a person with reduced mobility, then two reasons it matters. 2025 Q2: the importance of two of safety training, health and safety officer and risk assessment audit, one risk for each of three tasks, then two guidelines for each task.
questionTypes.marked: 2025 Q2: (a) 12 marks, 6 per item. (b) 12 marks, 4 per risk. (c) 36 marks, six guidelines at 6 marks each (3 for the note, 3 for the sketch). Sketches with typical dimensions are expected when the question says so.
questionTypes.play: Sketch every guideline with a number on it, for example a 1200 mm turning circle or a 900 mm door width. For a health and safety question, name the task, then the risk, then the control.
traps: Writing notes and no sketch in (c). Half of the 36 marks are for the sketches.
Naming a safety rule in general terms with no link to the task asked about.

questionTypes.name: U-value and heat loss calculation
questionTypes.where: Question 5 in 2024, 2025 and 2026. Always a wall build-up, then a cost, then an insulation thickness.
questionTypes.see: 2025 Q5: the U-value of a wall with render, external insulation, block and plasterboard. Then the annual cost of heat loss using wood pellets, then the extra insulation needed to reach 0.11 W/m2 C. 2026 Q5 used a timber frame wall with a sketch about moisture build-up.
questionTypes.marked: 2025 Q5: (a) 33 marks, 11 lines of 3 marks (every layer, both surface resistances, total resistance and the U-value). (b) 15 marks, 5 steps of 3. (c) 12 marks, 4 steps of 3. You get 3 marks for each correct line even if a later line goes wrong.
questionTypes.play: Set it out as a table: layer, thickness, conductivity, resistance. Do R = thickness divided by k for each layer, then add them. Then U = 1 divided by R. Show every step with its unit.
traps: Leaving out the two surface resistances. Each is a 3 mark line.
Forgetting the unit on the final answer. The scheme names W/m2 C or W/m2 K.
Putting thickness in millimetres into R = T/k. Convert to metres first.

questionTypes.name: Wall and roof construction comparison
questionTypes.where: Question 4 (2025 external walls; 2026 upgrading a 130 year old railway keeper's cottage).
questionTypes.see: 2025 Q4: three functional requirements of an external wall, two high performance wall constructions, then one advantage and one disadvantage of each. 2026 Q4 asked how to upgrade a heritage cottage while keeping its character.
questionTypes.marked: 2025 Q4: (a) 18 marks, 3 per note and 3 per sketch for three requirements. (b) 30 marks, each wall 5 for notes, 6 for the sketch, 2 for where the insulation goes and 2 for dimensions. (c) 12 marks, 3 per advantage or disadvantage.
questionTypes.play: Draw two walls you know well, with the insulation clearly marked and dimensioned. Write advantages and disadvantages that are specific, such as thickness, cost or moisture risk.
traps: Forgetting to mark the position of the insulation. It was 2 marks per wall.
Giving the same advantage for both walls.

questionTypes.name: Sustainability and discussion
questionTypes.where: Questions 6 and 10 (2025 Q6 low environmental impact and Q10 passive house; 2026 Q6 low impact house and Q10 indoor air quality).
questionTypes.see: 2025 Q6: three low-impact features with notes and sketches, three features of a healthy indoor environment, two benefits of locally sourced materials. 2025 Q10 had an alternative: discuss that the historic built environment is critical in addressing climate change, then give three guidelines to reuse historic buildings. 2026 Q10 gave an extract on building materials and health.
questionTypes.marked: 2025 Q6: (a) 30 marks, 5 for notes and 5 for a sketch per feature. (b) 18 marks, 6 per item (3 point, 3 discussion). (c) 12 marks, 6 each. 2025 Q10 alternative: 3 x 10 for the discussion (5 point, 5 discussion) and 3 x 10 for guidelines.
questionTypes.play: Use the pattern of point then discussion: one sentence naming the point, one or two saying why it matters. Link every point back to the house or material in the question.
traps: Stating a point without discussion. The scheme splits the marks evenly between point and discussion.
Answering a topical statement with general opinions instead of construction facts such as embodied carbon or retrofit.
